about: Where the readings of a Sunday or major feast meet in the Bible's own cross-references, and a Father's comment on the Gospel. Built by scripts/launch/make-readings-together.ts.

sources.xrefs: OpenBible.info cross references (CC BY 4.0); votes are community relevance scores, not Church teaching
sources.quoted: The app's own notes on New Testament quotations of the Old (public/data/lens/quotes.json)

2026-01-01.title: Solemnity of Mary, the Holy Mother of God

quote.author: Theophylact
quote.label: Theophylact
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: As men who were truly watching, they said not, Let us see (the child; but) the word which has come to pass, i.e. the Word which was from the beginning, let us see how it has been made flesh for us, since this very Word is the Lord. For it follows, Which the Lord has made, and has shown to us; i.e. Let us see how the Lord has made Himself, and has shown His flesh to us.

quote.author: Leo the Great
quote.label: Leo
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: Thou art troubled, Herod, without cause. Thy nature cannot contain Christ, nor is the Lord of the world content with the narrow bounds of thy dominion. He, whom thou wouldest not should reign in Judaea, reigns every where.

quote.author: Theophylact
quote.label: Theophylact
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: The Lord, placing before them, first, what is most profitable, that is, the food of the word of God, afterwards also gave the multitude food for their bodies; in beginning to relate which, the Evangelist say, "And when the day was now far spent, His disciples came unto Him, and said, This is a desert place.

quote.author: Theophylact
quote.label: Theophylact
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text:
But when He had dismissed the crowd, He goes up to pray, for prayer requires rest and silence.

Bede, in Marc., 2, 28: Not every man, however, who prays goes up into a mountain, but he alone prays well, who seeks God in prayer. But he who prays for riches or worldly labour, or for the death of his enemy, sends up from the lowest depths his vile prayers to God.

quote.author: Origen
quote.label: Origen
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: The Lord having overcome the tempter, power was added to Him, i.e. as far as regards the manifestation of it. Hence it is said, And Jesus returned in the power of the Spirit.

quote.author: Ambrose of Milan
quote.label: Ambrose
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: The fourth miracle after Jesus came to Capernaum was the healing of a leprous man. But since He illumined the fourth day with the sun, and made it more glorious than the rest, we ought to think this work more glorious than those that went before; of which it is said, And it came to pass, when he was in a certain city, behold a man full of leprosy.

quote.author: Augustine of Hippo
quote.label: Augustine
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: Our Lord did not baptize with the baptism wherewith He had been baptized; for He was baptized by a servant, as a lesson of humility to us, and in order to bring us to the Lord’s baptism, i.e. His own; for Jesus baptized, as the Lord, the Son of God.

quote.author: Jerome
quote.label: Jerome
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text:
Also that by being Himself baptized, He might sanction the baptism of John.

Chrys., Hom. 12: But since John’s baptism was to repentance, and therefore shewed the presence of sin, that none might suppose Christ’s coming to the Jordan to have been on this account, John cried to Him, "I have need to be baptized of Thee, and comest Thou to me?"

quote.author: Origen
quote.label: Origen
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: After this testimony, Jesus is seen coming to John, not only persevering in his confession, but also advanced in goodness: as is intimated by the second day. Wherefore it is said, The next day John sees Jesus coming to him.

quote.author: Jerome
quote.label: Jerome
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: Some of the less learned brethren suppose the Lord to have spoken what follows from the Mount of Olives, which is by no means the case; what went before and what follows fixes the place in Galilee - Mount Tabor, we may suppose, or any other high mountain.

2026-02-02.title: Feast of the Presentation of the Lord

quote.author: Augustine of Hippo
quote.label: Augustine
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: By the world here we must not understand heaven and earth, but the men who are in the world; or those who love the world for whose enlightenment the Apostles were sent.

quote.author: Jerome
quote.label: Jerome
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: This was allowed under the Law, as to children; as they offered sacrifice to God, that they might not do it to idols, so they were permitted to swear by God; not that the thing was right, but that it were better done to God than to daemons.

quote.author: Jerome
quote.label: Jerome
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: An arrogant and vain vaunt; for he hath not the power to bestow all kingdoms, since many of the saints have, we know, been make kings of God.

quote.author: Jerome
quote.label: Jerome
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: While they thought only of an earthly tabernacle of boughs or tents, they are overshadowed by the covering of a bright cloud; "While he yet spake there came a bright cloud and overshadowed them.

quote.author: Augustine of Hippo
quote.label: Augustine
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: The woman here is the type of the Church, not yet justified, but just about to be. And it is a part of the resemblance, that she comes from a foreign people. The Samaritans were foreigners, though they were neighbors and in like manner the Church was to come from the Gentiles, and to be alien from the Jewish race.

quote.author: Augustine of Hippo
quote.label: Augustine
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: Will you also? i.e. I am already, do you wish to be? I see now, but do not envy. He says this in indignation at the obstinacy of the Jews; not tolerating blindness, now that he is no longer blind himself.

2026-03-19.title: Solemnity of Saint Joseph, Spouse of the Blessed Virgin Mary

quote.author: Jerome
quote.label: Jerome
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: This passage is objected to us by the Emperor Julian in his Discrepancy of the Evangelists. Matthew calls Joseph the son of Jacob, Luke makes him the son of Heli. He did not know the Scripture manner, one was his father by nature, the other by law.

quote.author: Augustine of Hippo
quote.label: Augustine
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: Of the four days many things may be said. They refer to one thing, but one thing viewed in different ways. There is one day of death which the law of our birth brings upon us. Men transgress the natural law, and this is another day of death. The written law is given to men by the hands of Moses, and that is despised - a third day of death.

2026-03-25.title: Solemnity of the Annunciation of the Lord

quote.author: Ambrose of Milan
quote.label: Ambrose
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: But all are not as Mary, that when they conceive the word of the Holy Spirit, they bring forth; for some put forth the word prematurely, others have Christ in the womb, but not yet formed.

2026-03-29.title: Palm Sunday of the Lord's Passion

links.note: The cry from the cross opens Psalm 22, a prayer that moves from abandonment to praise. Mark 15:34 keeps the Aramaic.

quote.author: Origen
quote.label: Origen
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: Thus do the Gentiles shew favours to those whom they subject to themselves, until their yoke is riveted. Yet did this practice obtain also among the Jews, Saul did not put Jonathan to death, because all the people sought his life.

2026-04-03.title: Good Friday of the Lord’s Passion

quote.author: Augustine of Hippo
quote.label: Augustine
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: It was a band not of Jews, but of soldiers, granted, we must understand, by the Governor, with legal authority to take the criminal, as He was considered, and crush any opposition that might be made.

2026-04-04.title: Holy Saturday At the Easter Vigil in the Holy Night of Easter

quote.author: Jerome
quote.label: Jerome
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: Or, otherwise; This apparent discrepancy in the Evangelists as to the times of their visits is no mark of falsehood, as wicked men urge, but shews the sedulous duty and attention of the women, often going and coming, and not enduring to be long absent from the sepulchre of their Lord.

quote.author: Augustine of Hippo
quote.label: Augustine
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: Mary Magdalene, undoubtedly the most fervent in love, of all the women that ministered to our Lord; so that John deservedly mentions her only, and says nothing of the others who were with her, as we know from the other Evangelists.

2026-04-12.title: Second Sunday of Easter (or Sunday of Divine Mercy)

quote.author: Theophylact
quote.label: Theophylact
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: Or because He waited till all were assembled: and with shut doors, that he might show how that in the very same way he had risen again, i.e. with the stone lying on the sepulcher.

quote.author: Augustine of Hippo
quote.label: Augustine
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: The fortress mentioned here we may not unreasonably take to have been also called according to Mark, a village. He next describes the fortress, saying, which was from Jerusalem about the space of sixty stades, called Emmaus.

quote.author: Augustine of Hippo
quote.label: Augustine
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: Or thus: Many go under the name of good men according to the standard of the world, and observe in some sort the commandments of the Law, who yet are not Christians. And these generally boast of themselves, as the Pharisees did; Are we blind also?

quote.author: Augustine of Hippo
quote.label: Augustine
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: Our Lord consoles His disciples, who, as men, would be naturally alarmed and troubled at the idea of His death, by assuring them of His divinity: Let not your heart be troubled: you believe in God, believe also in Me; as if they must believe in Him, if they believed in God; which would not follow, unless Christ were God.

2026-05-31.title: The Solemnity of the Most Holy Trinity

quote.author: Hilary of Poitiers
quote.label: Hilary
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: If it were only a creature given up for the sake of a creature, such a poor and insignificant loss were no great evidence of love. They must be precious things which prove our love, great things must evidence its greatness. God, in love to the world, gave His Son, not an adopted Son, but His own, even His Only Begotten.

2026-06-07.title: The Solemnity of the Most Holy Body and Blood of Christ

quote.author: Augustine of Hippo
quote.label: Augustine
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: Or thus: Whereas men desire meat and drink to satisfy hunger and thirst, this effect is only really produced by that meat and drink, which makes the receivers of it immortal and incorruptible; i.e. the society of Saints, where is peace and unity, full and perfect. On which account our Lord has chosen for the types of His body and blood, things which become one out of many.

2026-06-12.title: Solemnity of the Most Sacred Heart of Jesus

quote.author: Jerome
quote.label: Jerome
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: That the burden of sin is heavy the Prophet Zachariah bears witness, saying, that wickedness sitteth upon a talent of lead. [ Zec 5:7 ] And the Psalmist fills it up, "Thy iniquities are grown heavy upon me."

quote.author: Jerome
quote.label: Jerome
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: A kind and merciful Lord and Master does not envy His servants and disciples a share in His powers. As Himself had cured every sickness and disease, He imparted the same power to His Apostles. But there is a wide difference between having and imparting, between giving and receiving.

quote.author: Jerome
quote.label: Jerome
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: How is it then that in the present world, the sins of so many are unknown? It is of the time to come that this is said; the time when God shall judge the hidden things of men, shall enlighten the hidden places of darkness, and shall make manifest the secrets of hearts.

quote.author: Jerome
quote.label: Jerome
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text:
Wherein He calls the Apostles to breaking of bread, that the greatness of the miracle might be more evident by their testimony that they had none.

Aug., De Cons.

2026-08-06.title: Feast of the Transfiguration of the Lord

quote.author: Jerome
quote.label: Jerome
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: While they thought only of an earthly tabernacle of boughs or tents, they are overshadowed by the covering of a bright cloud; "While he yet spake there came a bright cloud and overshadowed them.

quote.author: Jerome
quote.label: Jerome
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: Leaving the Scribes and Pharisees and those cavillers, He passes into the parts of Tyre and Sidon, that He may heal the Tyrians and Sidonians; "And Jesus went thence, and departed into the coasts of Tyre and Sidon."

quote.author: Jerome
quote.label: Jerome
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: This Philip was the brother of Herod, the tetrarch of Ituraea, and the region of Trachonitis, who gave to the city, which is now called Panaeas, the name of Caesarea in honour of Tiberias Caesar.

quote.author: Jerome
quote.label: Jerome
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: If then your brother have sinned against you, or hurt you in any matter, you have power, indeed must needs forgive him, for we are charged to forgive our debtors their debts. But if a man sin against God, it is no longer in our decision. But we do all the contrary of this; where God is wronged we are merciful, where the affront is to ourselves we prosecute the quarrel.

quote.author: Jerome
quote.label: Jerome
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text:
For it is customary with the Syrians, especially they of Palestine, to add a parable to what they speak; that what their hearers might not retain simply, and in itself, the instance and similitude may be the means of retaining.

Origen, (vid.

2026-09-14.title: Feast of the Exaltation of the Holy Cross

quote.author: Augustine of Hippo
quote.label: Augustine
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: Many dying in the wilderness from the attack of the serpents, Moses, by commandment of the Lord, lifted up a brazen serpent and those who looked upon it were immediately healed. The lifting up of the serpent is the death of Christ; the cause, by a certain mode of construction, being put for the effect.

quote.author: Gregory the Great
quote.label: Gregory
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: The morning is that age of the world which was from Adam and Noah, and therefore it is said, "Who went out early in the morning to hire labourers into his vineyard." The terms of their hiring He adds, "And when he had agreed with the labourers for a denarius a day."

quote.author: Jerome
quote.label: Jerome
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: Thus much prefaced, the Lord brings forward a parable, to convict them of their irreligion, and shew them that the kingdom of God should be transferred to the Gentiles.

quote.author: Jerome
quote.label: Jerome
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: Lately under Caesar Augustus, Judaea, which was subject to the Romans, had been made tributary when the census was held of the whole world; and there was a great division among the people, some saying that tribute ought to be paid to the Romans in return for the security and quiet which their arms maintained for all.

quote.author: Jerome
quote.label: Jerome
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: The Pharisees having been themselves already confuted (in the matter of the denarius), and now seeing their adversaries also overthrown, should have taken warning to attempt no further deceit against Him; but hate and jealousy are the parents of impudence.

quote.author: Jerome
quote.label: Jerome
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: Some of the less learned brethren suppose the Lord to have spoken what follows from the Mount of Olives, which is by no means the case; what went before and what follows fixes the place in Galilee - Mount Tabor, we may suppose, or any other high mountain.

2026-11-02.title: The Commemoration of All the Faithful Departed

quote.author: Theophylact
quote.label: Theophylact
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: He does not say, I am the bread of nourishment, but of life, for, whereas all things brought death, Christ has quickened us by Himself. But the life here, is not our common life, but that which is not cut short by death: He that comes to Me shall never hunger; and, He that believes in Me shall never thirst.

quote.author: Hilary of Poitiers
quote.label: Hilary
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text:
"Then," because all this discourse is concerning the great day of the Lord, concerning which He had been speaking before.

Greg., Hom. in Ev., xii, 1: By "the kingdom of heaven" is meant the present Church, as in that, "The Son of Man shall send forth his angels, and they shall gather out of his kingdom all things that offend."

quote.author: Origen
quote.label: Origen
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: He travels, not according to His divine nature, but according to the dispensation of the flesh which He took upon Him. For He who says to His disciples, "Lo, I am with you always, even unto the end of the world," [ Mat 28:20 ] is the Only-Begotten God, who is not circumscribed by bodily form.

quote.author: Theophylact
quote.label: Theophylact
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: The Lord wishing to prevent His disciples from asking about that day and hour, says, "But of that day and that hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels which are in heaven, neither the Son, but the Father."

quote.author: Ambrose of Milan
quote.label: Ambrose
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: But all are not as Mary, that when they conceive the word of the Holy Spirit, they bring forth; for some put forth the word prematurely, others have Christ in the womb, but not yet formed.

quote.author: Origen
quote.label: Origen
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: This is the second testimony of John the Baptist to Christ, the first began with, This is He of Whom I spoke; and ended with, He has declared Him.

2026-12-27.title: The Holy Family of Jesus, Mary and Joseph

quote.author: Origen
quote.label: Origen
quote.work: Catena Aurea (St. Thomas Aquinas, quoting the Fathers)
quote.text: If we marvel to hear that a woman was healed by touching the hem of a garment, what must we think of Simeon, who received an Infant in his arms, and rejoiced seeing that the little one he carried was He who had come to let loose the captive! Knowing that no one could release him from the chains of the body with the hope of future life, but He whom he held in his arms.
